open_questions.question: How complete must trace capture be before the learning loop stops producing regressions (e.g., the coding-agent brittleness after a few commits)?
open_questions.research_direction: Ablate trace granularity (final outcome only vs. tool calls vs. subagent trees) and measure downstream regression rate after successive commits.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The failure mode is asserted but no threshold, capture granularity, or measurement protocol is provided.

project_ideas.based_on: learning signal is destroyed if intermediate tool calls and subagent failures are discarded
project_ideas.hypothesis: Increasing trace capture granularity from outcome-only to tool-call level to full subagent execution trees monotonically reduces multi-commit regression rate in a coding agent after successive training rounds, with a measurable threshold below which added trace noise reverses the gain.
project_ideas.measurement: Regression rate per commit index per granularity level, plus improvement in rolloutable-eval pass rate and the cost/latency overhead of each capture depth.
project_ideas.name: Trace-Granularity Ablation Bench
project_ideas.poc: Instrument one coding agent to emit three parallel trace streams at increasing granularity over the same task distribution; run identical continual-learning cycles per stream and replay the same task set after each commit sequence; plot regression rate against capture depth and against added-noise volume.

project_ideas.based_on: Evaluations must be 'rolloutable': sampled from the real distribution of production tasks
project_ideas.hypothesis: An eval harness that reconstructs production starting states and samples the live task distribution predicts post-update production performance significantly better than a static benchmark suite, and the predictive gap widens as domain-specific experience accumulates.
project_ideas.measurement: Rank correlation between gate decision and post-deploy production outcome, false-ship and false-block rates, and the divergence between benchmark delta and production delta over successive training rounds.
project_ideas.name: Replay-Eval Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a replayer that snapshots and restores real user starting states, sample tasks from captured production traces, and run the same set of model/harness updates through both the replay harness and a static benchmark; compare predicted versus observed production outcomes.

project_ideas.based_on: Harnesses must co-evolve with models and contain domain knowledge
project_ideas.hypothesis: Moving a defined capability from hard-coded orchestration into model weights (or vice versa) produces a predictable cost/latency/retrainability outcome, and a light, open harness outperforms a hard-coded workflow harness after N co-evolution rounds.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success and regression rate per round, inference cost and latency per task, and the size of the training delta needed to absorb each migrated capability into weights.
project_ideas.name: Weights-vs-Workflow Splitter
project_ideas.poc: Take one agent task with a workflow-style harness, enumerate steps, and produce paired variants where each step lives in code versus weights; train both variants on the same trace corpus across several rounds and compare on rolloutable evals.

project_ideas.based_on: How should differential privacy and per-customer data isolation be enforced when training on multi-tenant production traces?
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-customer trace isolation plus a bounded privacy budget can be enforced without collapsing per-customer improvement, and there exists a measurable isolation granularity (trace-level vs. tenant-level) where learning signal per customer remains positive while cross-tenant leakage is eliminated.
project_ideas.measurement: Per-tenant eval delta versus a non-isolated control, privacy budget consumed per unit of learning signal, and leakage-probe success rate across isolation granularities.
project_ideas.name: Isolated Trace Trainer
project_ideas.poc: Split a multi-tenant trace corpus into isolated shards with configurable privacy noise budgets; train per-tenant adapters alongside a shared baseline, then measure per-customer improvement plus a leakage-attack probe against the shared components.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Arjun Karanam
  • Channel: Sequoia Capital
  • Main topic: Continual learning platforms for AI agents
  • Purpose: To introduce Trajectory's platform for continual learning and explain how companies can build AI agents that improve with use over time. Arjun Karanam, co-founder of Trajectory, discusses the concept of continual learning for AI agents. He explores why current frontier models optimize purely for IQ without experience, the economic value of experience, and how Trajectory is building a platform that turns every interaction into continually improving systems through traceability, evaluations, model behavior specs, and iterative RL training.

Topic Map

The Experience Gap in Frontier AI Models

  • Explanation: Frontier AI models are optimized for high IQ (PhD level) with zero experience, resembling a brilliant new hire on day one. However, the economy values experience deeply, creating an 'Experience Gap' that companies must close.
  • Key claims:
    • Frontier labs optimize solely for IQ.
    • Today's agents are slow, expensive, and error-prone.
    • The economy values 30-year domain experience much more than raw intelligence alone.
  • Examples:
    • Terence Tao arriving day one at an accounting firm vs. a 30-year expert accountant.
  • Terminology:
    • frontier models
    • IQ axis
    • experience gap
    • orthogonal axis of experience
  • Why it matters: Models must gain real-world experience through continual learning rather than remaining static and expensive.

Unlocking Real-World Interaction Data

  • Explanation: Billions of tokens are generated daily by AI agents in production, but most of this real-world signal goes to waste. Trajectory aims to treat real-world interactions as the primary signal for continual learning.
  • Key claims:
    • 100 billion tokens per day are generated by production AI.
    • Most interaction signals currently go to waste.
    • Learning from real-world interactions mimics how humans get smarter.
  • Examples:
    • Weekly usage of models across OpenRouter growing rapidly.
  • Terminology:
    • tokens/day
    • product telemetry
    • real-world signal
  • Why it matters: Real-world interactions provide the training data needed to make models efficient, reliable, and continuously improving.

The Trajectory Platform Solution

  • Explanation: Trajectory's platform bridges the gap through four main pillars: traceability, model behavior specs, model optimization, and harness co-evolution.
  • Key claims:
    • Traceability requires capturing full traces plus product telemetry including subagents.
    • Evaluations must represent the full distribution of tasks and outcomes.
    • Models should be better, cheaper, and faster.
    • Harnesses must co-evolve with models and contain domain knowledge.
  • Examples:
    • Harvey lab benchmark integration with 1,760 tasks.
  • Terminology:
    • traceability
    • SDPO
    • model behavior spec
    • harness
    • rolloutable evals
  • Why it matters: Providing a structured product layer allows companies to own their own experience layer and continuously improve agents.

Key Points

The Economy Values Experience

  • Explanation: Companies pay most for personnel with decades of domain experience, not just raw intelligence.
  • Evidence: Comparison between Terence Tao on day one at an accounting firm vs. an experienced accountant.
  • Practical implication: AI agents must transition from static tools to continuous learners that compound in value with use.

Capturing Full Traces and Subagents

  • Explanation: Traceability must capture entire execution trees including subagents, rather than throwing away intermediate tool calls.
  • Evidence: Coding agents frequently break after a few commits if subagent failures are discarded.
  • Practical implication: Build error-correction, edits, and retries natively into product interfaces to capture clean training signals.

Making Evals Rolloutable

  • Explanation: Evaluations must reflect real production traffic and allow full replay of user starting states.
  • Evidence: Static benchmarks do not represent actual user workflows and requests.
  • Practical implication: Sample real distribution of tasks and ensure evaluation harness matches production.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Trajectory Continual Learning Framework

  • How it works: Captures user interactions, defines model behavior specs, optimizes models and harnesses jointly, and deploys updates instantly.
  • Components:
    • Traceability
    • Model Behavior 'Spec'
    • Evaluations
    • Models
    • Harness
  • When to use: When deploying AI agents in production that need to improve autonomously over time.

Examples & Case Studies

Harvey integrated with Trajectory to manage benchmark testing across 1,760 tasks.

  • Illustrates: Easy import, model training, evaluation comparison, and one-click deployment of fine-tuned models.
  • Lesson: Continual learning infrastructure can reduce post-training and deployment workflows to minutes.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Capture full execution traces including subagents in your AI product.
    • Design products with native affordances for edits, undos, and retries to generate clean supervision labels.
    • Build evaluation harnesses that match production traffic distributions.
  • Strategic:
    • Every company should own its own experience layer that never stops evolving.
    • Move away from hard-coded workflows toward light, open, and informative harnesses.
    • Transition from closed hosted models to training on open-weight models to unlock autonomous improvement.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How do we handle differential privacy and customer data isolation during continual learning?
    • What role does episodic memory play in updating agent behavior after corrections?
    • How do we weight human feedback versus automated task completion signals in RL credit assignment?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Every company should own its own experience layer that never stops evolving. (strategic vision)
  • Training models on domain expertise matches large general models at a fraction of the cost. (economic claim)

Notable Quotes

"Frontier models feel like a brilliant new hire, on their day one of the job." (at 0:56) "Trajectory turns every interaction into continually improving systems." (at 5:05) "You can only improve what you can see." (at 10:11) "Every company should own its own experience layer that never stops evolving." (at 23:36)

Compressed Summary

  • Frontier AI models suffer from an Experience Gap, optimizing for IQ without real-world experience.
  • Trajectory provides infrastructure for continual learning via traceability, evals, model specs, and harnesses.
  • Capturing full traces and subagent interactions is essential for extracting learning signals.
  • Running on open weights allows companies to continuously train and deploy improved agent models.
  • Keywords: continual learning, ai agents, traceability, reinforcement learning, harness
  • Core insight: AI agents must transition from static, pre-trained tools into systems that continuously learn and compound in value from every real-world user interaction.

- **Explanation**: Companies pay most for personnel with decades of domain experience, not just raw intelligence.
- **Evidence**: Comparison between Terence Tao on day one at an accounting firm vs. an experienced accountant.
- **Practical implication**: AI agents must transition from static tools to continuous learners that compound in value with use.
### Capturing Full Traces and Subagents
- **Explanation**: Traceability must capture entire execution trees including subagents, rather than throwing away intermediate tool calls.
- **Evidence**: Coding agents frequently break after a few commits if subagent failures are discarded.
- **Practical implication**: Build error-correction, edits, and retries natively into product interfaces to capture clean training signals.
### Making Evals Rolloutable
- **Explanation**: Evaluations must reflect real production traffic and allow full replay of user starting states.
- **Evidence**: Static benchmarks do not represent actual user workflows and requests.
- **Practical implication**: Sample real distribution of tasks and ensure evaluation harness matches production.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Trajectory Continual Learning Framework
- **How it works**: Captures user interactions, defines model behavior specs, optimizes models and harnesses jointly, and deploys updates instantly.
- **Components**:
  - Traceability
  - Model Behavior 'Spec'
  - Evaluations
  - Models
  - Harness
- **When to use**: When deploying AI agents in production that need to improve autonomously over time.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Harvey integrated with Trajectory to manage benchmark testing across 1,760 tasks.
- **Illustrates**: Easy import, model training, evaluation comparison, and one-click deployment of fine-tuned models.
- **Lesson**: Continual learning infrastructure can reduce post-training and deployment workflows to minutes.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Capture full execution traces including subagents in your AI product.
  - Design products with native affordances for edits, undos, and retries to generate clean supervision labels.
  - Build evaluation harnesses that match production traffic distributions.
- **Strategic**:
  - Every company should own its own experience layer that never stops evolving.
  - Move away from hard-coded workflows toward light, open, and informative harnesses.
  - Transition from closed hosted models to training on open-weight models to unlock autonomous improvement.
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - How do we handle differential privacy and customer data isolation during continual learning?
  - What role does episodic memory play in updating agent behavior after corrections?
  - How do we weight human feedback versus automated task completion signals in RL credit assignment?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- Every company should own its own experience layer that never stops evolving. (strategic vision)
- Training models on domain expertise matches large general models at a fraction of the cost. (economic claim)
## Notable Quotes
> "Frontier models feel like a brilliant new hire, on their day one of the job." (at 0:56)
> "Trajectory turns every interaction into continually improving systems." (at 5:05)
> "You can only improve what you can see." (at 10:11)
> "Every company should own its own experience layer that never stops evolving." (at 23:36)
## Compressed Summary
- Frontier AI models suffer from an Experience Gap, optimizing for IQ without real-world experience.
- Trajectory provides infrastructure for continual learning via traceability, evals, model specs, and harnesses.
- Capturing full traces and subagent interactions is essential for extracting learning signals.
- Running on open weights allows companies to continuously train and deploy improved agent models.
- **Keywords**: continual learning, ai agents, traceability, reinforcement learning, harness
- **Core insight**: AI agents must transition from static, pre-trained tools into systems that continuously learn and compound in value from every real-world user interaction.
